verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that Chakasaponin Ii may interact with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3 through multiple indirect pathways. The first pathway links Chakasaponin Ii to 11-cis retinol dehydrogenase, which in turn targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The second pathway connects Chakasaponin Ii to CMP-N-acetylneuraminate-beta-1,4-galactoside alpha-2,3-sialyltransferase, which is also targeted by Cycloleucine, which itself targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The third pathway involves a more complex compound that ultimately targets the same transporter. These findings collectively indicate that Chakasaponin Ii may influence the activity of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3 through a series of molecular interactions, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated. The evidence is consistent across different pathways, suggesting a potential role for Chakasaponin Ii in modulating the function of this transporter, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct relationship.
